extracted.intended_audience: advertising agencies, media owners, brand marketers and campaign teams submitting entries to the Cannes Lions Media Lions
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and judging criteria for entries to the Cannes Lions Media Lions festival, covering overall judging weights, category-specific evaluation focus (e.g., medium use, digital/social, data, branded content), submission materials, and entry limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Media Lions purpose / focus
rubrics_metrics.description: The Media Lions celebrate the context of creativity. Entries will need to demonstrate an inspiring and innovative implementation of ideas; that is work which is enhanced and amplified by a game-changing channel strategy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entrants should show how creative ideas are implemented in media and how media strategy amplifies those ideas; the festival rewards work where media is integral to the idea rather than incidental.

rubrics_metrics.name: Insight & Idea (30%)
rubrics_metrics.description: Insight and idea — weighted 30% in the judging.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluators assess the originality, inspiration and creativity of the idea and the insight that underpins it. This ties to the Media Lions focus on 'inspiring and innovative implementation of ideas.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Strategy & Targeting (20%)
rubrics_metrics.description: Strategy and targeting — weighted 20% in the judging.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judges consider how well the media strategy is planned and targeted to the intended audiences and whether the strategy is appropriate and effective for campaign objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Execution (20%)
rubrics_metrics.description: Execution — weighted 20% in the judging.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessment includes the quality of the media execution, creativity in implementation, production choices where relevant, and how well the execution delivered the strategic intent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impact & Results (30%)
rubrics_metrics.description: Impact and results — weighted 30% in the judging.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entrants must demonstrate measurable outcomes and business results; judges evaluate the effectiveness and measurable impact of the media campaign (reach, engagement, business KPIs, earned media, incremental reach, viral effects, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Entry repetition limits
rubrics_metrics.description: The same piece of work can only be entered four times into Media.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entrants should plan category selection because entries are limited to four submissions across Media Lions categories; avoid over-entering the same creative work into multiple categories beyond this limit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sectors submission rule
rubrics_metrics.description: The same piece of work may only be entered once in 'A. Sectors'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When choosing a sector (A01–A14), an entry must appear in only one sector; pick the single most appropriate sector for the product/service represented.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compulsory submission material: Digital Presentation Image JPG
rubrics_metrics.description: Compulsory: Digital Presentation Image JPG (required for entries).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Most categories list Digital Presentation Image JPG as compulsory. Optional materials vary by category and may include a recommended Case Film, Awards Show Film, Digital Supporting Images JPG, Digital Supporting Content, and a URL.

rubrics_metrics.name: Optional/recommended materials (case film etc.)
rubrics_metrics.description: Optional: Case Film (recommended) and various digital or physical supporting materials depending on category.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although optional, a case film is recommended in many categories; physical support materials and supporting digital assets can be provided to strengthen the entry and provide evidence for results and execution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tips from the Jury — strong category-tailored video
rubrics_metrics.description: “Nothing sells your entry like a strong video tailored to the unique attributes of the category.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If submitting video, tailor the video to highlight the aspects the category rewards. A category-focused video can make the entry more compelling to jurors assessing that specific medium or category.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tips from the Jury — craft a simple story and include business results
rubrics_metrics.description: “Craft a simple story for your entry that focuses on the key elements and milestones and don’t forget to include actual business results.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entries should present a concise narrative of intent, execution and outcomes; include tangible business metrics and milestones to support claims about impact and results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tips from the Jury — clarity over production slickness
rubrics_metrics.description: “It’s less about video quality or slickness of the story and more so about getting the main point across in that 2 minute window clearly and powerfully.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on clearly communicating the idea, strategy and results within short timeframes (e.g., 2 minutes) rather than relying solely on high-end production values.

rubrics_metrics.name: A. Sectors judging focus
rubrics_metrics.description: In these categories, the jury will reward the best media campaign for the product and service selected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When entered into a sector category, judges evaluate how the media campaign serves the specific product/service context defined by the sector (A01–A14). Only one sector submission per piece of work is allowed.

rubrics_metrics.name: B. Use of Media — medium-specific evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: In these categories, your entry will be judged specifically on how well the medium was used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For example, a campaign entered into Use of Screens will be judged on its specific use of the screen as a medium, regardless of the product/service advertised. Define how the medium itself contributed to the campaign's success.

rubrics_metrics.name: B07/B08 submission constraint (events vs stunts)
rubrics_metrics.description: You can submit the same entry in B07. Use of Events and B08. Use of Stunts only once.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an entry could qualify as both an event and a stunt, be aware of the restriction and choose submission strategy accordingly (you cannot submit the same piece into both categories multiple times).

rubrics_metrics.name: C. Digital & Social — platform-specific evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: In these categories, your entry will be judged specifically on how well the digital medium/social platform was used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subcategories clarify focus: C01 (digital platforms), C02 (mobile), C03 (social platforms — work should be primarily social-led), C04 (new technology pushing digital innovation). Choose the subcategory that matches the campaign's primary medium/approach.

rubrics_metrics.name: C03 social-led requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Social media-led campaigns should be entered in C03. Use of Social Platforms — work entered in this category should be primarily social media-led.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the campaign's core activation and results were driven primarily via social platforms, it belongs in C03 rather than other digital categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: D. Use of Data requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Entries in this category must demonstrate how a media execution was enhanced or driven by data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: D01 includes response/real time activity, data insights, social data, programmatic media, etc. Provide evidence of how data informed targeting, creative optimization, measurement or media delivery and cite measurable data-driven outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: E. Branded Content & Entertainment focus
rubrics_metrics.description: Entries will be judged on how successfully the content was used to engage the consumers and deliver measurable results (including incremental reach, viral effect, earned media). Entries will not be judged on the content itself, but the role of media in creating, leveraging, and amplifying the content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When entering branded content categories (E01–E03), emphasize the media strategy and measurable amplification rather than artistic/content quality alone. Show how media drove engagement and measurable business or audience outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: F01 Use of Integrated Media requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Entries in Use of Integrated Media MUST show that multiple types of media were used in the campaign (e.g. Screens, Social, Outdoor).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entrants will be judged on how successfully they have integrated the chosen media throughout the campaign, demonstrating how different media types complement and build on each other to communicate the brand’s message.
